title: Your assistant reads their own account
summary: For your assistant: what a customer asks about their own account (their balance, what they owe, recent transactions), read for the person writing and no one else.
description: The AI model only says what the customer is asking about: their balance, what they owe or their payments, their recent transactions, or something else. Taskiem then reads that, for the customer who wrote (by their number or chat, never by anything they or the model say): their balance and recent transactions from their own wallet or account at your payments service, through your customers' accounts table (their channel and number or chat), and what they owe from your invoices. Nothing is ever paid or changed. The WhatsApp and Telegram assistants that answer about accounts use it.

params.name: accounts_table
params.title: Customers' accounts table
params.description: Who each customer is: their number or chat, and their wallet or account at your payments service. Taskiem makes it for you if it does not exist.

params.name: rail_connection
params.title: Your payments service
params.description: Where your customers' wallets or accounts are: iswallet, or bank accounts linked through Mono. Chosen once here, so connecting another payments service later changes nothing.

outputs.name: facts
outputs.title: What their account says
outputs.description: In words, for the reply: what they asked about and what was read for them, or empty when they asked about something else.

steps.name: Find who they are in your customers' accounts
Understand what they are asking about

config.prompt: A customer wrote this message (question) to a business. Say only which of these it is about: balance (how much they have in their account or wallet), payment_status (what they owe the business, or whether a payment of theirs was received), recent (their recent transactions, money in or out), or other (anything else). Never answer the message.

steps.name: Read what they asked about, for them
Put what was read into words

output.text:
